exp/p2ride.problem: P2: the obstacle-free 13 km ride has 45 false alarm events, 38 STOP episodes and 183 alarm frames at baseline P3d. The five empty recordings have 13 events and 16 episodes. The target was at most 30 ride events with every positive preserved.

best.description: A learned track-level second opinion. The model is 60 depth-3 gradient-boosted trees (35 KB of JSON, evaluated with numpy). It scores a track when the rules are about to make it a STOP. The score uses 19 features taken from the track's last 10 matched clusters: range, lateral position and its spread/jumps, centroid-z spread, height/length/width statistics, share of voxels inside the envelope, demotion/column/beyond-trust shares, roughness of the distance series, hit count and hit fraction. Point-count, visibility and train-speed features were dropped because the injector produces them artificially. A track with a probability below 0.0225 that is beyond 25 m is held as advisory (CAUTION, reason 'doubt') for 10 more matched STOP-qualifying frames. With doubt_sticky the score at the onset decides, and a withheld track is released immediately if it comes within 25 m. It never vetoes and never takes a confirmed STOP down. Training data: negatives are the rules' STOP rows on the ride (8 gate pieces) and the five empty recordings. Positives are synthetic objects ray-cast into real ride frames: 8 kinds on 12 moving files, plus 6 kinds with the train standing on 7 files. Validation is grouped: each ride piece or empty recording is held out together with the synthetic sequences injected into it (held-out AUC 0.964). The threshold is the highest at which no held-out synthetic sequence is delayed, so it has zero margin on that data. Set O, doubleT_obstacle and 10 synthetic crossing-person sequences were never trained on; none of their onsets is delayed.

exp/p2ride.tradeoffs: The cost is a safety trade-off. A track that is doubtful and beyond 25 m reaches STOP 10 matched frames (about 1 s at 10 Hz) later than now, and shows CAUTION in the meantime. That is the case whenever the model is wrong about a real object. On every positive measured it never fired: set O, doubleT_obstacle (real person and rail object at 56 m with the train standing), set F, 101 held-out synthetic sequences and 10 held-out crossing persons. But the threshold has zero margin on the held-out synthetic data: the lowest synthetic onset score is 0.0226 against a threshold of 0.0225. All positives are either synthetic or the single real recording, and a real object shaped unlike the training kinds (person, boxes of 0.3-1.0 m, trolley, cable, 0.3x0.3x0.1 low box, rail object, dog) may be delayed. The 25 m near range is a policy choice; I measured 20, 25 and 30 m in the replay. Monitoring cost: withheld STOPs become CAUTION, adding up to 3.4 pp newly uncertain frames on squareT_platform, 0.58 pp on doubleT_platform and 0.66 pp on the ride, with no clear_distance loss. The model is trained on this detector's own outputs, so it must be retrained whenever an upstream stage changes the tracks it sees. The gate_along_x association fix (idea c) removes only 3 more alarm frames on top of c1 and was not gated.

exp/p2ride.recommendation: Adopt c1 (the five tracking.doubt_* keys above) as the P2 candidate. It is the only screened candidate: the full screen passes the gate and meets the target (ride 45 -> 24 events, 38 -> 28 STOP episodes), with every positive row identical and fewer history-stress STOPs (78 -> 47). Before shipping it as default, a safety reviewer should accept the 1 s CAUTION delay beyond 25 m for low-opinion tracks. Retrain the model after merging with other experimenters' changes, and widen the synthetic kinds (irregular debris, lying person, fallen panel) to build a margin under the threshold, since it currently has none on the synthetic data. Treat gate_along_x as optional: only a 3-frame extra gain, not gated.
exp/p2ride.ml_used: A track-level gradient-boosted classifier: scikit-learn GradientBoostingClassifier with 60 trees, depth 3, subsample 0.8, class-balanced, used for training only. It is exported to 35 KB of JSON and evaluated with pure numpy/python at run time (about 0.3 ms per evaluation, only at STOP onsets; no measurable per-frame latency change). Training rows are the rules' STOP-candidate rows. Negatives: 212 rows from the ride and the five empty recordings. Positives: 2,597 rows from 101 synthetic sequences ray-cast into real ride frames, both moving and standing train. Validation is grouped leave-one-group-out over the 8 ride pieces and 5 empty recordings, each synthetic sequence held out with its ride piece (held-out AUC 0.964). The threshold is the highest that delays no held-out synthetic sequence. Set O, doubleT_obstacle and 10 synthetic crossing persons are pure test sets: 0 onsets delayed. The learned score is used only to require more persistence, never as a veto, and never within 25 m.

exp/p1edge.problem: P1: the organizers' edge objects in set O got a STOP only at about 5-10 m. #4 small_edge_inside had 2 STOP frames from 5.2 m and #6 big_edge_inside had 6 frames from 10.3 m. The organizers placed the objects from the SENSOR X axis, while the detector measures the envelope from the rails. On every recording (and the ride) the rails run at -0.25 +- 0.03 deg to the sensor axis on straight track; I measured the per-frame median yaw of the baseline outputs. Two shape rules then block the objects: #4 is demoted as `floating` because its outermost point is beyond floating_free_max_dy 0.95, and #6 is dropped by the wall rule (|lateral| > 1.2 and taller than 1.9 m).

best.description: M5. Near the train on straight track, the envelope is measured from the sensor axis (the organizers' placement frame). Conditions: rail pair locked, |curvature| <= 2e-4, X <= 60 m. The rail-to-sensor offset is clamped to 0.2 m, so the frame switch is continuous and never moves the envelope more than 0.2 m. This replaces the rails; it is not a union. The strict membership and the shape rules read the sensor-frame lateral. The rules for structure along the track (linear infrastructure and the edge signature) keep reading the rail lateral. The rails also keep: the candidate set, the reported lateral, the gauge-distance reach, the rails' own strict mask (used by the oversize-split fallback and the wall keep), and the bed, low-object, rail-start, ego-speed, hanging-search and clear-cap stages. In addition, the existing floating exemption for compact free-hanging clusters is widened from an outermost point of 0.95 m to 1.2 m, which is still inside the 1.40 m advisory corridor. The full screen ran on commit c03b5cd; HEAD 6e74cb3 has identical code and adds only tests and config comments.

exp/p1edge.ml_used: None. The problem is which coordinate frame defines 'inside' (rails or the organizers' sensor axis; organizer question Q1 is unanswered), not a classification problem. A learned edge-object versus infrastructure model would also need ride cluster-level negatives and synthetic edge positives, evaluated on held-out ride pieces and set O. Extracting those needs roughly 50 minutes of ride replay per variant on this loaded 4-CPU machine, and screens took 18-35 minutes each with 4-6 in the queue. So I kept to a geometric, config-switchable change. The rail-to-sensor heading was estimated from the data (median yaw -0.25 deg across all recordings and ride pieces) and used to justify the offset limits.
exp/p1edge.tradeoffs:
1. It is not a union. Within 60 m on straight track the strict envelope moves up to 0.2 m toward the sensor axis. On these rigs (rails at -0.25 deg), between about 45 and 60 m the right-hand envelope edge moves in by up to 0.2 m, so an object up to 0.2 m inside the rails' envelope there is only CAUTION until it is nearer. The left edge gains the same amount. test_not_a_union pins this behaviour down. Physically the train sweeps the rail envelope; the organizers' hidden data is placed in the sensor frame.
2. doubleT_obstacle (rig yaw -1.16 deg, so the clamp applies): the person crossing from the left STOPs 3 frames earlier. An object coming from the right would be later by the same geometry.
3. The union review's safety scene (a box touching a 30 m edge line) holds. Without the rails-mask fallback it lost 19 -> 7 STOP frames; with it, the reference keeps every STOP.
4. Limits: #6 is caught only from about 28-30 m. Its face touches the edge, and beyond about 45 m the 0.2 m clamp is smaller than the true 0.27-0.35 m offset. Clamp 0.3 (M4) catches #4 from 47.9 m but was never screened on the ride.
5. #7's false STOP at 142 m stays. Only the full-range clamp (M2) removes it, and that costs ride events (84 m and 94 m).
6. Scorer limitation, reported and not fixed: resense.metrics.match uses a 1 m lateral tolerance around the label centre, not widened by half the object's width. A 2 m box whose only in-corridor part is its inner strip (1.2-1.3 m from the rails, label centre 2.2-2.4 m) is unmatched in most STOP frames. Under the gate's scorer #6 shows 7 frames; the track STOPs in 15-16. Changing the scorer would change every baseline row.
7. Accumulation: if frame eligibility flips (straight to curve) within the 5-frame buffer, buffered far points (>= 40 m) can be misplaced laterally by up to the clamp for up to 0.5 s.

exp/p3over.problem: P3: /resense/clear_distance overclaims range past objects inside the envelope. On set O, 46 frames have decision GO while an in-envelope object is nearer than clear_distance - 0.5 m (54 counting all decisions). The limits for fixing it are at most 5 pp newly-uncertain frames and a median clear_distance of at least 95% of baseline, for each of the five empty recordings and for the ride. best.description:
Two new opt-in caps on clear_distance. Both are off by default, so the defaults reproduce P3d exactly. Neither changes a detection, a track, the health level or the decision.

(1) health.clear_cap_thin, the M2 predicate without its CAUTION. It caps at the nearest scan-line cluster (the tracking.stop_keep_thin kind) that meets all of these: zone gauge, n_gauge >= cluster.gauge_min_points, reason empty, kind empty, n_acc == 1, and within the trusted range min(valid, floor_valid) captured before clustering. Its set O output matches the M2 observer captures frame for frame.

(2) health.clear_cap_persist = k, implemented as PersistentEvidence in the new module resense/evidence.py. Each frame it takes the non-low corridor returns inside the nominal envelope polygon, i.e. the rail envelope without the lateral edge margin, so the margin acts as a band rather than a hard cut. It groups them into sparse blobs:
- linked at 0.45 m x (1 + X/100);
- compact: at most 0.5 m in every direction, or a single scan line up to 2.1 m wide;
- at least 2 returns;
- isolated: at most 10 other corridor returns within 2 m along the track. A per-return prefilter drops crowded stretches before linking.

A blob is chained to a previous-frame blob that has the same lateral offset (within 0.12 m) and height (within 0.2 m), lies 0.5-3.0 m farther, and whose own shift differs by at most 0.08 m. That is a static object approaching at a constant apparent speed, with no speed input needed. A chain of k = 4 frames caps at the blob's nearest return.

Cost measured offline on the dumps: 0.5 ms mean and about 1 ms p95 per frame; the maximum was about 10 ms, measured while the machine load average was about 20.

The sub-keys persist_min_points, persist_max_extent, persist_row_height, persist_row_width, persist_max_around, persist_shift, persist_tol_dy, persist_tol_h and persist_tol_shift are all documented in configs/default.yaml and in the identical ros2_ws/src/resense_ros/config/detector.yaml. Their defaults are the recommended values.

GO overclaims 46 -> 16; target 54 -> 24 (GO 16 / CAUTION 6 / STOP 2); intent 223 -> 183. Newly-uncertain frames 0 pp everywhere. Median clear_distance retained: doubleT_platform 1.0, roundT_doubleT 0.9598 (135.5 -> 130.05 m), roundT_pressureGate 1.0, roundT_squareT 0.9805, squareT_platform 1.0, ride 0.9804 (122.6 -> 120.2 m). The P1 edge, P2 ride, five-empty, set O STOP, doubleT_obstacle and P4 history blocks are byte-identical to the baseline (78 history STOP events).

The 16 GO overclaims that remain:
- small_center, 10 frames:
  - 291: no return inside the fitted nominal envelope; its returns sit 0.34-0.62 m below the fitted rail head at 127 m, beyond the 120 m height reference.
  - 303 and 308: first sightings after gaps; frames 304-307 have no envelope return.
  - 310-312: the chain is still building (depth 1-3 of the 4 needed).
  - 315-318: at 315 the far axis shifted the blob laterally by 0.17 m, more than the 0.12 m tolerance, which broke the chain. It rebuilt over 316-318 and caps again from 319 to 336.

exp/p3over.tradeoffs:
- The binding constraint is roundT_doubleT, at 95.98% against the 95% limit. On 5 frames above its median, the estimate is now capped at a fragment where the extrapolated straight corridor meets a curved tunnel wall. At 55-120 m this fragment looks exactly like the set O cube, both geometrically and in its motion.
- Every stronger setting failed that recording: chain length 3, coasting, gap-skipping, looser tolerances, and the learned scorer at useful thresholds.
- The tolerances were chosen with the five empty recordings and set O in view. The ride was evaluated for only three settings, so it serves as the held-out check (98.0%).
- The last 16 GO overclaims are structural limits of a causal 4-frame chain: first sightings, chain build-up, one lateral jump of the far axis, and evidence below the envelope floor or beyond the trusted range. Closing them would need an axis model that stays stable at 100 m or a lower chain length, and a lower chain length costs range on roundT_doubleT.
- The screen's latency rows read 5x worse because the machine was running at load average 15-20. They are informational and not caused by this change; offline the evidence update costs about 0.5 ms mean and 1 ms p95.
- The caps add conservatism only (shorter clear_distance); they never lengthen it and never change a decision.

exp/p3over.recommendation: Adopt health.clear_cap_thin=true and health.clear_cap_persist=4 as the new defaults, keeping the persist_* sub-keys at their shipped defaults. This cuts GO overclaims 46 -> 16 within every acceptance limit, changes no detection, and passed the full gate. Do not lower clear_cap_persist or loosen the tolerances: roundT_doubleT is at 95.98%. The learned scorer, coasting and gap-skipping stay off; they were evaluated and are documented above. Re-screen once it is combined with any axis or corridor candidate.
exp/p3over.ml_used: Yes, experimental and not shipped. A logistic-regression scorer for sparse envelope blobs used 12 features: log range, |dy|, height, return count, extents, isolation, strict fraction, chain depth, shift residual and scan-line flag. Positives were synthetic: 0.3 m cubes ray-cast into 24 moving sequences of the ride (473 blobs). Negatives were 45k blobs from the five empty recordings and the 8 ride pieces. Validation used grouped held-out folds (recording or sequence), giving AUC 0.936. It was then tested as a range cap on the organizers' set O, which was never used in training. As a cap it gave GO 30-37 within the limits, or failed roundT_doubleT at lower chain lengths. That is not better than the physically-motivated chain rule, so it was not shipped. Its strongest weight is on range, which partly reflects how the injections were sampled.

best.description: c10. Three opt-in keys; each default is off and reproduces the P3d baseline. (1) cluster.column_width_trim=0.05: the column rule measures width between the 5% and 95% quantiles of the cluster's lateral point positions. The bbox is no longer used, so a few returns joined at the DBSCAN radius can't push a column past 1.0 m (mechanism 2: 7 of 143 returns had widened a 0.74 m column to 1.10 m). (2) track.axis_disagree_hold=5: after a frame whose two boundaries disagree, the 60 m disagreement cap stays on for 5 nominal periods on frames that fit only one boundary. Two agreeing boundaries end it. So losing the contradicting boundary no longer jumps the trust from 60 to 120 m (mechanism 1). This is a bounded version of the rejected T1. (3) tracking.gate_along_only=true: the ego_speed_max x dt approach allowance widens the association gate along the track only. It used to widen it in every direction (2.5 m at 10 Hz, 7.5 m after two dropped frames), which joined unrelated clusters metres apart across the track. Each of (1) and (2) removes the failed_clear and old_stock STOPs on its own (exact float-bag replays). Proposed defaults: exactly these three values.

exp/p4hist.tradeoffs:
The captured failure is fixed, and both mechanisms have an independent fix. The broader goal of no STOP in a seeded history that the every-frame history doesn't also produce is not met under the gate: history-only events went from 26 to 24.

Most of those residual events confirm on thin evidence. The confirmation rule counts sensor time (confirm_time_s), so a track with dropped frames can confirm on 3 hits with a 2-of-3 zone vote, where every frame needs 5 hits. Examples: roundT_doubleT drop40 at 137.6 m, doubleT_platform drop40 at 88 m and 3.0 m, roundT_pressureGate catchup at 86-92 m.

The rules that remove these cost positives:
- tracking.zone_min_votes=5 (78 -> 70 with the other keys) delays set F person and trolley at ~150 m by one frame.
- tracking.start_clean (-> 63) delays one set F person sequence from 166 to 151 m.
- tracking.confirm_hits=5 delays two set O objects by one frame.

The reason is that the offline caches carry bursty receive stamps (0.2-0.45 s, then 0.02 s). Set F's far detections on the ride therefore also confirm on 3 hits with 2-of-3 votes, and the detector cannot tell that apart from dropped frames. On regular header stamps (the node) this conflict should shrink; I have not measured that.

axis_disagree_hold=5 costs 4.5% of median clear_distance on squareT_platform (limit 5%). Its other effects are not isolated from the other two keys (in combination the ride falls 41/33/162 vs 44/38/180 and 43/35/175 for the other keys alone). Dropping it still fixes both captures through the column trim alone, but loses the fix for mechanism 1.

The remaining every-frame false STOPs are unchanged: squareT_platform's structure at 82.9 m with 2-4 strict voxels at the envelope edge, its 145-147 m face, and doubleT_platform's young-bed low clusters at 30-40 m. They account for most of the history total.

No ML component was trained. With the time and a machine lock shared by several experimenters, I had no way to validate a learned confirmation model against the gate, which forbids losing a single set O STOP frame.

exp/p4hist.recommendation:
Adopt c10 as new defaults: tracking.gate_along_only=true, cluster.column_width_trim=0.05, track.axis_disagree_hold=5. The full gate passes, the captured clear-run STOP is gone from all three node histories, and the ride drops from 45/38 to 41/33 events/episodes with no loss on any positive.

If the 4.5% range cost on squareT_platform is judged too close to the 5% limit, ship gate_along_only and column_width_trim only. The column trim alone still removes both captured STOPs and gives ride 43/35.

Keep zone_min_votes, start_clean and confirm_hits=5 off. They buy another 8-15 history events but each delays a far or small positive by a frame.

The next step for P4 is to check the confirmation conflict on header-stamped replays before revisiting those rules: re-run set F and the ride with the gate's --nominal-stamps option (evenly spaced stamps in place of the cache's bursty receive stamps), or on node captures. The residual history STOPs need sensor-frame-based evidence (hits per sensor frame, not per receive-time second), which is only separable from dropped frames with regular stamps.
exp/p4hist.ml_used: none. A learned confirmation classifier was considered and set aside: no held-out validation against the strict per-frame positive gate was possible in the time and lock budget.

exp/p5range.problem: P5 detection range. On set O the organizers' objects are visible well beyond the first STOP. Far away, the part of an object inside the envelope is often a single scan line: the 2x0.2 m plank at 85-100 m, or the lower edge of the 2x2 m box at the envelope top at 103-125 m. That line is flatter than cluster.min_height and was dropped, so it never made a track. The 0.3 m cube gives 4 voxels at 60-75 m, one under the 5-voxel bar, and was dropped as well.

best.description: Far, sparse evidence counts only for a track that is approaching the train. Two kinds of evidence are affected: scan lines (corridor clusters flatter than min_height) that are 60 m or more away, inside the strict envelope with at least 4 strict voxels and overlapping no other cluster; and clusters under the point-count bar with at least 4 voxels, 60 m or more away, in zone gauge. Both go to the tracker only. There they may start or continue a track, but only when the evidence is unambiguous: it lies inside the gate of exactly one track and that track is unmatched in this frame; if it lies inside no gate it starts a new track; otherwise it is ignored. A track that ever used this evidence becomes a STOP only while it is approaching. The test is a line fit of its last 5 distances against sensor time: slope between -25 and -2 m/s, RMS residual at most 0.5 m. Such a track that was not reported stays unreported. One reported as advisory stays advisory. A track that was a STOP in the previous frame keeps the usual rules. The reasoning: a scan line of the bed or the vault stays fixed relative to the sensor, or jumps several metres with the pitch, while a static object ahead approaches at the train's speed along a straight line. All new keys are off by default, and the defaults reproduce the baseline exactly. Proposed defaults: thin_far_min_distance 60, weak_min_points 4, with thin_far_min_voxels 4, approach_hits 5, approach_min_speed 2.0 and approach_max_residual 0.5 left as they are.

exp/p5range.tradeoffs:
- **The gains are real but modest.** The mechanism only adds frames where some part of the object is inside the envelope as a scan line or a 4-voxel cluster.
- **big_above at 121-160 m is out of reach.** Its bottom is 3.2-3.7 m by the model. The vault cross-check agrees with the model to within 0.1-0.3 m up to about 110 m in those frames, so the box probably really is above the 3.0 m top there.
- **The plank beyond 100 m and the cubes beyond ~60 m are out of reach too.** The plank reads below the envelope floor. The cubes give 2-4 returns at the envelope edge, where they are demoted by floating / free_max_dy and the strict edge margin.
- **The approach test does not separate static infrastructure from obstacles.** Both approach at train speed. It removes only artefacts that are fixed to the sensor or jump with the pitch.
- **At a standing train, far evidence never creates a STOP.** A far object seen only as scan lines or weak clusters ahead of a stopped train stays unreported or advisory. That is no worse than the baseline, which drops that evidence entirely.
- **The three refinements are in-sample on the ride.** "No takedown", "unambiguous association" and "never promote an advisory report" were written after seeing three specific ride events (piece 6 at 115-118 m, piece 7 at 96-98 m, piece 2 at 96.8 m). They are general tracking rules, but their ride result should be treated as in-sample. The five empty recordings, set O, set F and the history stress were not used to design them.
- **Side effects on existing false tracks.** One ride false STOP (piece 6, frame 1346) starts one frame earlier; another loses 5 frames and one episode (piece 5, frames 302-306). Net ride alarm frames 183 -> 180, STOP episodes 38 -> 37, events unchanged at 45.
- **Latency.** The extra per-frame work is a few far clusters plus a 5-point line fit per track. The gate's latency rows are dominated by machine contention (4 parallel experimenters) and are not comparable.
- **No ML was used.** A learned far-field gate would have to train on synthetic positives. The false events it would need to remove are the same few ride events already handled in-sample, and EXPERIMENTS §8 explains why a learned veto on synthetic positives is the weakest link. The remaining limits are the height reference and the physics (2-4 returns), which a classifier cannot supply.
